summary: ITER151 · Runtime State Hardening — VERIFIED. Frontend 7-state ModuleRouteGuard pass-through works for all 6 critical operational routes at desktop AND mobile viewports. LOADING pass-through verified (no blocked-state flash during 3s hard-refresh sample window). Backend pytest regression 19/19 PASS. Atelier Media Direction signed URLs intact (Supabase signed URL, complete=True, 1920x1097). Architectural files present (CoreAutoRecoveredBadge.jsx, ModuleLoadingState.jsx, ModuleBlockedState.unavailable variant). NOTE: the CORE_AUTO_RECOVERED diagnostic badge could NOT be triggered via the malicious feature_flag insertion technique because the BACKEND resolver pre-empts the frontend by auto-forcing dashboard back to `enabled` (we confirmed this by direct call to resolve_modules — backend logs `core_critical_safety event=resolver_auto_force code=dashboard attempted_state=hidden`). This is the defense-in-depth contract working as designed (backend safety first, frontend safety as second line). The frontend CORE_AUTO_RECOVERED branch is code-evident in ModuleRouteGuard.jsx (lines 107-118) and CoreAutoRecoveredBadge.jsx exists; the branch will fire only when backend safety regresses.

issues: Many i18n missing string warnings (nav.crm_accounts, nav.journey_index, nav.runtime.loading, taxonomy.journey_lifecycle_studio.* etc) emitting on every page load; pre-existing, not from this iter, but noisy
React warning: 'Cannot update a component while rendering a different component' — pre-existing setState-in-render warning

CORE_AUTO_RECOVERED.scenario: set tenant_configuration.feature_flags={'dashboard':'hidden'} on studio tenant, restart backend, navigate to /dashboard logged in as admin@
CORE_AUTO_RECOVERED.explanation: Backend resolver auto-forces dashboard back to `enabled` before bundle reaches the browser; logs emit 'core_critical_safety event=resolver_auto_force code=dashboard attempted_state=hidden'. Frontend never sees a non-operational state for `dashboard`, so the frontend CORE_AUTO_RECOVERED branch never fires. This is the correct defense-in-depth contract.
CORE_AUTO_RECOVERED.cleanup_applied: feature_flags reverted to {} and backend restarted

action_items: OPTIONAL · The CORE_AUTO_RECOVERED frontend branch is currently unreachable via the documented test technique because backend safety pre-empts it. If E1 wants to E2E-verify the frontend safety net, they could (a) ship a transient backend flag to skip auto-force for one tenant, OR (b) add a unit test that mounts ModuleRouteGuard against a stub useModule() returning a non-operational state for a core code and asserts the badge testid renders. Recommended: option (b) — fast and avoids touching prod paths.

OPTIONAL · Address the noisy i18n missing-key warnings (nav.runtime.loading, nav.crm_accounts, nav.journey_index, nav.crm_follow_ups, nav.crm_archived, nav.language_cc, nav.settings_workspace, nav.blueprint_admin, taxonomy.journey_lifecycle_studio.*) — these emit on every page load and dilute genuine warning signal.
critical_code_review_comments: ModuleRouteGuard.jsx 7-state machine is clean, explicit, and disjoint — no implicit fallback path. Branch ordering is correct (LOADING → UNKNOWN_CODE → OPERATIONAL → CORE_AUTO_RECOVERED → BLOCKED → UNAVAILABLE).
FRONTEND_CORE_CRITICAL set (dashboard, settings_workspace, blueprint_admin, begin_journey, journey_index, team) correctly mirrors the backend allow-list per the iter146 review.
CoreAutoRecoveredBadge correctly gates on NODE_ENV !== 'production' OR localStorage flag — preview build is development so it WILL render when the branch fires.
ModuleBlockedState.VARIANT_META.unavailable copy is in Italian per user-language requirement.
Minor: warn() helper short-circuits in production — good. Could be extended to a structured telemetry sink later but not required for this iter.
seed_data_creation: Transiently set tenant_configuration.feature_flags={'dashboard':'hidden'} on the studio tenant, then reverted to {} after the CORE_AUTO_RECOVERED probe. Backend restarted twice (set + revert) to invalidate the resolver cache.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend resolver's core-critical safety pre-empts the frontend CORE_AUTO_RECOVERED branch. To E2E-exercise the frontend branch you must bypass backend safety (e.g. temporarily mark dashboard as is_core_critical=FALSE in feature_modules_registry, set feature_flag override, then re-enable). Cleanest path is a Jest/React Testing Library unit test mounting ModuleRouteGuard with a mocked useModule.
rca of the issue: N/A — no defect found. The badge non-appearance during the malicious-feature-flag probe is expected behavior given backend safety runs first.
